evidence: Source positive: frozen tests/test.sh:60-61 initializes zero reward and EXIT trap; :68-83 rejects missing entry/symlink escape; :104-111 runs app with sanitized env and uid 65534; :115-124 probes before RewardKit; :212-227 runs gates then scored and score.py after each successful suite. bash -n passed; task test.sh and frozen template are byte-identical (SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa). Defect: tests/test.sh:33-39 sends TERM once then waits without a bound for the original app child. Isolated Linux/POSIX probe at per-row-review/evidence/21/cleanup-wait-result.json confirms a TERM-resistant child held wait until watchdog KILL at three seconds. The initialized zero/reward file does not ensure a completed verifier rollout when cleanup stalls. This is an isolated shell proof, not an exact-current configured judge run; no row-relevant full-run evidence exists. See per-row-review/evidence/21/source-audit.md. Three sampled raw-index artifact hashes matched, but they describe scripted golden/application checks only.
counterexample: A submitted Node server fully serves the requested app but installs a SIGTERM-ignoring handler. After RewardKit exits, the verifier's EXIT trap waits indefinitely on that child; the outer 13,200-second deadline may end the rollout before its valid score is returned. A no-server broken app correctly retains the initial zero, so that negative path does not hide this exit defect.
suggested_fix: Bound cleanup: TERM the app process group, allow a short grace interval, KILL a still-live group, reap it, and preserve the already written reward and original exit status; test both resistant parent and child.
